text: Authors of typeset formulas augment those formulas to make them easier to understand. When they do so, they trade off between using markup tools like LaTeX and formula-unaware graphical editors. In this paper, we explore how editing tools could combine the best affordances of both kinds of tools. We develop FreeForm, a projectional editor wherein authors can augment formulas—with color, labels, spacing, and more—across multiple synchronized representations. Augmentations are created graphically using direct selections and compact menus. Those augmentations propagate to LaTeX markup, which can itself be edited and easily exported.
